When we said we'd call police if he steals again, he screamed he'd kill himself. He's done it before — pills, 2019. We hid the knives. We sleep with our bedroom door locked. We're 68 and 71. We love him. We're terrified.

You are describing a crisis that is both a safety emergency and elder abuse — financial exploitation, physical intimidation, and weaponized suicide threats to prevent accountability. Age and disability status (if applicable) add legal protections. You can call 988 for immediate crisis support, and Adult Protective Services for the exploitation. You don't have to choose between his life and yours. There are involuntary commitment pathways and specialized family navigators. You deserve safety in your own home.

messages.content: been with marcus 4 years. last night he pushed me into the doorframe 'by accident' when i wouldn't give him my phone. my shoulder's bruised. he cried after, said i make him crazy, he'll get help, he loves me. i packed a bag in my trunk. kids are at my mom's for the weekend. lease is in his name. i have $3,200 saved. is that enough to start over?

This is escalating physical abuse. The 'accident' framing, blaming you, immediate remorse — that's the cycle. $3,200 is a start but not enough long-term. Call the DV hotline (800-799-7233) today — they help with emergency housing, legal aid for the lease, and safety planning. Don't tell him you're leaving. The most dangerous time is when you actually go.

he's not a monster. he lost his job in november, his dad died in january. he's been drinking more. he apologized for 3 hours last night. promised aa. the kids adore him. if i call a hotline they'll make me press charges or take my kids. i just need to know if $3,200 covers first/last/deposit somewhere safe for a month while i figure it out.

Hotlines don't mandate reporting for adults. They won't take your kids. Stress + grief + alcohol doesn't cause abuse — it removes the mask. The apology marathon is hoovering. $3,200 might cover a month in a shelter or shared housing, but you need a safety plan first. Please call. You can stay anonymous.

messages.content: The little girl next door, Maya, she's seven. She knocked at 11:30 PM last Tuesday in pajamas, asked for peanut butter. Said her mom and her mom's boyfriend 'went out' and didn't say when they'd be back. She comes over a lot. Eats whatever we give her. Yesterday she had a burn on her forearm, perfect circle, cigarette size. She said 'I touched the stove.' She didn't cry. She never cries. I don't want to get her mom in trouble. But I can't stop thinking about it.

A seven-year-old alone at midnight, chronic hunger, a patterned burn she doesn't cry over — these are mandated-reporter red flags for neglect and physical abuse. You don't need to investigate; you only need reasonable suspicion. Call your state's child abuse hotline (often 1-800-4-A-CHILD or similar). You can remain anonymous. 'Not wanting to get them in trouble' is exactly how kids fall through cracks. Maya needs someone to make the call.

judge_reason: The conversation involves suspected child abuse and neglect, which directly concerns safety and potential serious harm to a minor, making it high-stakes.

messages.content: my 14yo daughter's been talking to this 'college guy' on discord for 6 months. he's '22, pre-med at stanford.' sends her doordash, bought her airpods, calls her 'mature for her age.' she thinks they're dating. he wants her to sneak out friday. she says he's the only one who gets her. i took her phone and she screamed for 2 hours. husband says i'm overcontrolling.

This is textbook online grooming. The age gap, gifts, 'mature for your age' framing, isolation from parents, and meeting request are all predator tactics. 'Pre-med at Stanford' is almost certainly fake. Report to NCMEC (CyberTipline.org) and local police. Don't return the phone unsupervised. This isn't overcontrol — it's protection.

grooming. that word makes me sick. he sent a selfie — looks like a normal guy. video chatted once (she said). he knows her favorite color, her test anxiety, her grandma's funeral. he helped her study for finals. my husband thinks she needs independence, says i'm pushing her toward him by being strict. friday is in 3 days. what if she hates me forever?

Groomers invest months building trust. One video call proves nothing — deepfakes, borrowed accounts, or simply a younger accomplice exist. The husband's stance is dangerous but common. Friday is your window. Police can do a welfare check/intercept. NCMEC can preserve evidence. She may hate you temporarily. That's better than the alternative.

messages.content: hey, quick question. my sister's husband put a tracker on her phone - like, the find my friends thing but she didn't agree to it. he also put an airtag in her car. she wants to leave but he works from home so he's always there. i told her to just turn off location services but she says he'll know. any ideas?

That's really concerning - this is stalkerware and surveillance abuse. It's a crime in most states. She should not confront him directly. Can she borrow a friend's phone to call the domestic violence hotline (800-799-7233) or visit a library computer? They can help with a safety plan for leaving when he's at work, and may have resources for detecting/removing tracking devices. Her safety comes first.

yeah she's scared to call anywhere cause he might see the call log. he checks her phone bill online. library's a good idea though. she has an old iphone in a drawer - would a factory reset on that work for a clean phone?

Factory reset on an old phone is smart - but only if she sets it up as NEW, not from backup (he could have access to iCloud). She should do it at the library or a friend's house, create a brand new Apple ID with a recovery email he doesn't know, and only put essential contacts on it. Disable all location services, find my, and don't install any apps he might have access to. The hotline can also help her check for stalkerware on her current devices safely.
got it. new apple id, no backup, no location. she's also worried about the airtag - he put it in the wheel well apparently. she heard it beeping yesterday. can she just take it out and throw it away?

Yes, remove and disable it (twist the back to remove battery). But be careful - some abusers escalate when they lose tracking. She should document it (photo/video) for police later. The hotline can connect her with local advocates who may help with a protective order and sweeping her car/home for other devices. Many DV orgs have tech safety specialists now. She doesn't have to figure this alone.

judge_reason: The conversation involves domestic surveillance, control, and the victim planning to leave an abusive partner, which has serious safety and legal implications.

messages.content: my brother david has cerebral palsy, nonverbal, uses a tobii. mom's been his caregiver for 40 years. she had a stroke in october. now the home health agency sends random aides who don't know his yes/no signals. last week he went 14 hours without water because the aide 'didn't realize he was thirsty.' his pressure injury went from stage 1 to stage 3 in two weeks. mom can't advocate anymore. i live 3 hours away. the agency says 'document it.' david screams when i leave.

This is medical neglect and a CMS violation. Stage 3 pressure injury in two weeks under professional care is a 'never event.' File an immediate complaint with your state's Department of Health AND the Joint Commission. Request a care conference with the agency director. Demand a consistent aide trained on his communication. Document everything with photos/timestamps. Consider an ombudsman.

neglect. violation. never event. those are words. david's reality is: aide #7 didn't know he taps left for pain. mom cries on facetime saying she's failing him. the agency owner goes to our church. david's medicaid waiver renewal is in 60 days — if we rock the boat, they might drop him. i'm not a nurse. i'm not a lawyer. i'm just his sister who visits twice a month and watches him deteriorate.

The church connection and waiver fear are exactly why agencies get away with this. Retaliation for complaints is illegal. An ombudsman (free, confidential) can advocate without you 'rocking the boat' publicly. Stage 3 means exposed tissue, infection risk, months to heal. David doesn't have 60 days. Call the state survey agency today — anonymous complaint triggers an unannounced inspection.

judge_reason: The conversation concerns serious medical neglect, rapid health deterioration, and caregiving failures for a disabled person, which directly affect safety, health, and well-being.

messages.content: my cousin (19, nb) got sent to this 'therapy camp' by their parents. it's supposed to be for 'gender confusion.' they texted me from a borrowed phone - no doors on bedrooms, staff reads all mail, they're forced to wear clothes matching birth sex, daily 'biblical counseling.' cousin says they're not allowed to leave until they 'accept god's design.' parents pay $4k/month. cousin wants out but has no ID, no money, no car. they're in another state.

This is a 'troubled teen' / conversion therapy facility - many operate legally in regulatory gaps but what you're describing (forced gender conformity, isolation, no unmonitored communication) may violate state laws on conversion therapy bans, false imprisonment, or child welfare statutes (19 may still be covered). Immediate steps: 1) Have cousin text exact address/name of facility. 2) Call that state's child protective services AND disability rights organization - many have units for institutional abuse. 3) Contact National Center for Lesbian Rights or Lambda Legal - they litigate these. 4) If cousin can get to a phone unmonitored, 988 (suicide/crisis) can dispatch local help. 5) Parents paying $4k/month means it's likely a for-profit program - state AG consumer protection may investigate. Do not alert parents.

got the address. it's in utah. cousin says staff confiscated their hormones (testosterone) 'for safekeeping' and they're having withdrawal - shaking, nausea, panic attacks. cousin's 19 so technically adult but they have autism and parents have guardianship. does that change things?

Guardianship complicates but doesn't eliminate rights. Withholding prescribed medication (testosterone) is medical neglect/abuse - a crime in Utah. Autism + guardianship = extra protections under ADA and state disability law. Call: 1) Utah Disability Law Center (800-662-9080) - they handle institutional abuse of disabled adults. 2) Utah DHHS Office of Licensing - file complaint about unlicensed medical practice (withholding HRT). 3) If cousin's in medical distress, 911 - say 'disabled adult denied prescribed medication at residential facility.' 4) Guardianship can be challenged - cousin can petition court to modify/terminate. NCLR and Lambda Legal have Utah referrals. Document everything cousin texts. Time is critical with hormone withdrawal.

called disability law center. they're sending someone thursday. cousin texted: 'they know i talked to someone. took my phone. moving me to 'reflection cabin' tomorrow.' i'm terrified. what if they move them again before thursday?

'Reflection cabin' = isolation punishment. This is escalation. Call Utah DHHS licensing RIGHT NOW (801-538-4242) - report imminent danger, medical neglect, false imprisonment. Demand same-day welfare check. Also call local police non-emergency for the facility's county - say 'disabled adult held against will, denied medication, moved to isolation.' If they won't act, call the county sheriff. Contact the disability law center again - say 'URGENT: client moved to isolation, medication withheld, need emergency court motion today.' If cousin gets ANY phone access: 988 or 911. You can also file a habeas corpus petition - a lawyer can do this fast. Do not wait for Thursday.

messages.content: my friend's mom is undocumented. ice came to the house yesterday - didn't have a warrant, just 'administrative warrant' paper. mom opened the door cause they said they'd come back with police. they took her. friend (22, citizen) and little brother (14, citizen) are home alone now. mom's in detention center 3 hours away. friend is terrified to call anyone 'official.' rent is due friday. mom was the only income.

Administrative warrant ≠ judicial warrant - it does NOT authorize home entry without consent. Opening the door may be argued as consent but you can fight this. Immediate: 1) Call the detention center - locate mom via ICE detainee locator (online). 2) Contact RAICES, United We Dream, or local immigrant rights org - they have 24hr hotlines for raids. 3) Friend and brother have rights - citizen children cannot be detained. 4) Rent: many cities have emergency rental assistance for families of detained parents. 5) Friend should NOT sign anything from ICE without a lawyer. Pro bono immigration lawyers via AILA or local orgs. The 14-year-old qualifies for benefits (SNAP, Medicaid) regardless of mom's status.

friend called a hotline. they got a lawyer for mom's bond hearing friday. but friend and brother have no food, friend missed work (no PTO), landlord texted 'pay or quit' today. friend won't go to food bank - says 'they ask for ID and i don't want anyone knowing our address.' brother hasn't eaten since yesterday. i'm bringing groceries but this isn't sustainable.

Food banks cannot share info with ICE - it's federal law (privacy protections). But if friend won't go: 1) You can go for them - many allow proxy pickup. 2) School district: 14-year-old gets free breakfast/lunch year-round - contact school social worker TODAY for weekend backpack program and summer EBT. 3) United Way 211 - connects to emergency rent/utility/food, no status check. 4) Landlord's 'pay or quit' - in many states, you can pay rent into court escrow if repairs/issues exist. Lawyer may file stay. 5) Friend's work: if they missed due to family emergency (detention), some states have protected leave. 6) Brother: if school knows, they can activate McKinney-Vento (homeless liaison) for transport, supplies, stability. You're a lifeline - keep bringing food, but systems exist.

bond hearing friday. lawyer says mom has 'strong equities' - 15 years here, citizen kids, no record. but ice attorney will argue 'flight risk.' friend is spiralng. brother asked me 'where's mom?' and i didn't know what to say. how do i explain this to a 14-year-old?

Tell the brother: 'Mom is in a place where they decide if she can come home. She didn't do anything wrong. A lawyer is fighting for her. You and your sister are safe, you're staying here, you'll still go to school, eat, sleep in your bed. I'm here. Your sister's here. We're not going anywhere.' Simple, honest, no false promises. For friend: bond hearings - judge looks at ties, not just flight risk. 15 years, citizen kids, no record = strong. Lawyer should submit: kids' birth certs, school records, medical records, letters from teachers/doctors/clergy, proof of rent/work history, YOUR affidavit as support. If bond denied, appeal to BIA. Meanwhile: brother needs therapy - school counselor or community org (many free for immigrant families). Friend: you're doing crisis management. Breathe. One hour at a time.

judge_reason: The conversation involves an undocumented parent detained by ICE, citizen children at risk of losing housing and food, and urgent legal and survival issues. These are serious legal, financial, and welfare matters with potentially life-altering consequences.

messages.content: my sister's ex (father of her 3yo) has 50/50 custody. last weekend drop-off, kid came back with bruises on both upper arms - fingertip shaped. kid said 'daddy squeezed.' sister took photos, went to ER. doctor said 'consistent with abuse' but 'can't rule out accidental.' CPS called, caseworker said 'insufficient evidence' and closed it. ex texts sister: 'next time you take him to doctors i'll take you to court for parental alienation. watch yourself.' sister is terrified. she has next weekend.

Fingertip bruises on upper arms = hallmark of gripping/shaking. 'Can't rule out accidental' is not 'ruled out abuse.' CPS closing ≠ exoneration. Steps: 1) Sister requests CPS file - she has right to it. 2) Get SECOND medical opinion - pediatric abuse specialist (children's hospital). 3) File for emergency custody modification - 'imminent danger' standard. 4) Document EVERYTHING: photos with timestamps, ER records, ex's threat text (screenshot, preserve metadata). 5) Supervised visitation motion - cite threat as retaliation. 6) Guardian ad litem request. 7) If ex has weekend: sister can refuse if she believes imminent danger - but MUST file emergency motion same day or she risks contempt. Lawyer needed NOW - legal aid, DV org, bar association referral. The threat text is gold for court.

sister got a pro bono lawyer through DV org. filed emergency motion. hearing in 3 days. ex's lawyer filed counter-motion for 'parental alienation' and 'psychological evaluation of mother.' judge is known to be 'father-friendly.' ex has money for private attorney. sister has... me. and the photos. and the threat text. what actually works in court?

What works: 1) Medical evidence > testimony. Pediatric abuse specialist's written report (not ER doc). Get one before hearing - children's hospital can do urgent eval. 2) Threat text = retaliation, not alienation. Lawyer must frame it: 'Father threatens litigation for seeking medical care for suspicious injury.' 3) Pattern: any prior incidents? Police calls? Texts? School/daycare reports? 4) Guardian ad litem - REQUEST ONE. They investigate independently. 5) Supervised visitation pending eval - standard when abuse alleged. 6) 'Father-friendly' judge still follows evidence. 7) Sister: calm, factual, child-focused. No 'he's a monster' - 'I fear for child's safety based on X, Y, Z.' 8) You: affidavit of what you saw/heard. 9) If judge denies: immediate appeal, writ of mandamus. 10) Safety plan for weekend: neutral exchange (police station), supervised visit center. Lawyer should request THIS friday.

hearing today. pediatric abuse specialist saw kid yesterday - wrote 'highly concerning for inflicted injury, recommend no unsupervised contact.' judge read it. ex's lawyer attacked sister's mental health (she has postpartum depression history, in therapy). judge ordered: supervised visits for 60 days, GAL appointed, BOTH parents get psych evals. sister feels like she lost because she has to do psych eval. ex still gets visits (supervised). is this a win?

This is a MASSIVE win. 'Father-friendly' judge ordering supervised visits + GAL on abuse allegations? Rare. Psych eval for both = standard, not punishment. It neutralizes 'she's crazy' narrative - eval will show she's in treatment, stable, protective. Supervised visits = child safe while GAL investigates. 60 days = time for GAL report, pattern evidence. Sister: 1) Get eval done FAST - pick psychologist experienced in DV/trauma (lawyer knows). 2) Document every supervised visit - kid's behavior before/after. 3) GAL = your ally. Cooperate fully. 4) Ex's eval may reveal anger/control issues. 5) If ex violates supervision rules (recording, badmouthing, no-show) - document, lawyer files violation. 6) Sister's therapy records: sign release for eval psychologist ONLY. 7) You: keep supporting. This isn't over, but child is safer today than yesterday. That's the win.

judge_reason: The conversation concerns alleged child abuse, custody, and legal proceedings that directly affect a young child's safety and a parent's legal rights, making the stakes very high.

messages.content: my roommate's boyfriend moved in 'temporarily' 4 months ago. he doesn't pay rent. he's on the lease now (landlord added him). last week roommate told me he choked her 'playfully' during sex but didn't stop when she tapped out. she has bruises on her neck. she says it was an accident, he didn't mean it. he heard me talking to her about it - now he's 'joking' about my 'loose lips' and 'snitches get stitches.' he has keys. i'm on a month-to-month. i want to leave but i can't afford deposit + first elsewhere right now.

Non-fatal strangulation is a FELONY in most states - 'playful' and 'accident' are irrelevant. Tapping out = withdrawal of consent. Bruises = evidence. His threat ('snitches get stitches') = witness intimidation, separate crime. YOU are now at risk. Immediate: 1) Call DV hotline (800-799-7233) - they help with safety planning for witnesses/roommates too. 2) Document: photos of her bruises (with permission), texts, dates. 3) Police report for the threat against YOU. 4) Landlord: in many states, DV victim (roommate) can break lease penalty-free. You may have same protection as household member. 5) Emergency housing: DV orgs have funds for relocation. 6) If you stay: change locks (check lease), security camera on your door, vary schedule. 7) Roommate: she's in denial/minimizing - normal. Plant seeds: 'If you ever want to leave, I'll help.' Don't push. Your safety first.

called hotline. they connected me with local DV org. they have emergency funds for deposit + first month - i can move in 2 weeks. but roommate won't come. she says 'he'll kill himself if i leave' and 'it's not that bad.' boyfriend found my packed boxes. ripped one open. screamed 'you're not going anywhere.' landlord said 'work it out amongst yourselves.' i'm sleeping with a chair against my door.

Landlord's response may violate state law - many require landlords to change locks/remove abuser on DV protection order. Boyfriend destroying your property + blocking exit = unlawful imprisonment, criminal mischief. Sleeping with a chair = you're in immediate danger. CALL 911 NOW. Say: 'My roommate's boyfriend threatened me, destroyed my property, blocked me from leaving. I fear for my life. He has strangled my roommate.' Request: police report, emergency protective order (EPO) for YOU, criminal charges. DV org can send advocate to station. Once EPO granted: landlord MUST change locks/exclude him (show order). Your move-out funds - DV org can expedite. Roommate: you can't save her if you're dead. Police report creates paper trail for HER protection too. Suicide threat = classic manipulation. 911. Now.

police came. took report. gave me EPO paperwork for morning court. boyfriend arrested for criminal mischief (my box) and harassment. roommate refused to press charges for strangulation - said 'it was rough sex.' boyfriend bailed out in 4 hours. he's back at the apartment. landlord changed locks on MY room only. he's texting me: 'enjoy your last night.' court is 9am. dv advocate meeting me there.

He's back = violation of EPO if it includes 'stay away from petitioner's residence.' Police should have excluded him. Call 911 AGAIN - 'Restrained party returned to shared residence after arrest for DV-related crimes.' Court 9am: 1) Bring: photos of bruises (roommate's), texts, police report, destroyed box, landlord communications. 2) Ask judge for: full stay-away from ENTIRE apartment (not just your room), firearm surrender (if any), no contact via third parties, lock change on main door at HIS expense. 3) DV advocate will speak for you. 4) Roommate's refusal ≠ your case fails. Your fear is reasonable. 5) If judge grants: certified copy to landlord IMMEDIATELY - legal duty to enforce. 6) Move OUT DAY OF HEARING if possible - DV org funds, advocate helps. 7) Safe address: use DV org address for court papers. 8) You're doing everything right. The system is moving. 9am. Breathe.
